question: Which national nutrition programme in India primarily provides mid-day meals to school children aged 6–14 years to improve nutritional status and school attendance?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: ICDS targets children aged 0–6 years and pregnant/lactating women, not primary school children.
Correct. PM POSHAN (renamed from the Mid-Day Meal Scheme in 2021) provides cooked meals to children in Classes 1–8, improving enrolment, attendance, and nutritional status.
WIFS provides weekly iron-folic acid tablets to adolescent girls and boys; it is a supplementation programme, not a meal programme.
NIDDCP focuses on universal salt iodization to prevent goitre and IDD; it does not provide meals to school children.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the national nutrition programmes section. PM POSHAN (previously the Mid-Day Meal Scheme) is the programme that provides cooked meals to school children in Classes 1–8.
Well done! PM POSHAN is the government's flagship school feeding programme covering government and government-aided schools.
